svg.title: The toolbox checks the test really failed first, instead of taking anyone's word for it: The test suite works only with the GitLab of its own project, and stops when that GitLab is missing
svg.text: The toolbox checks the test really failed first, instead
of taking anyone's word for it
Scenario: The test suite works only with the GitLab of its own project, and stops when that GitLab is missing
No GitLab of its own, no GitLab at all

g.text: Given two Docker Compose projects on the same machine each run a service called gitlab
One machine can run several Docker Compose projects at once: this toolbox, a project made from it, or an unrelated one.
Docker Compose labels each container with its project and its service, and two projects can both have a service called
Three throwaway containers set that scene. e2e-ours-gitlab-1 and e2e-neighbour-gitlab-1 stand in for the GitLabs of two
projects. e2e-ours-codeceptjs-1 stands in for the container that runs the test suite, in the project e2e-ours.
When the test suite asks for its GitLab, it gets the one of its own project
The test suite finds its GitLab with one helper, composeService, in project/tests/e2e/support/helpers/docker.js. The
helper reads the project of its own container, then asks Docker for the gitlab service of that project only.
Run in the suite's container, it answers e2e-ours-gitlab-1: the GitLab of its own project, not the neighbour's.
Then with its own GitLab stopped, the test suite refuses to use the neighbour's
docker stop prints the name of our GitLab, e2e-ours-gitlab-1, and only the neighbour's is still running. The same
question now gets a refusal instead of a name, in the helper's words: No "gitlab" service is running in the Compose
Stopping is the safe answer. The suite creates an admin token and registers runners on the GitLab it is given, so the
Off camera, a suite container whose project label is empty is refused too: the helper cannot tell which project is its
own, and it does not guess.
